messages.subject: Horizontal Legend
parts:
I was trying to reproduce this heat map of unemployment from WSJ
(http://datavisualization.ch/showcases/interactive-table-about-jobs-
outlook) using ggplot2. I was able to reproduce it almost similar to
the original graphic, except for the following issues:

1. I was unable to make the legend horizontal.
2. I was unable to move the x-axis labels to the top of the graph.

My question is, are (1) and (2) possible with the current options
available in ggplot2?

Thanks for reading.

Cheers.
Ramnath

> outlook) using ggplot2. I was able to reproduce it almost similar to
> the original graphic, except for the following issues:
>
> 1. I was unable to make the legend horizontal.
> 2. I was unable to move the x-axis labels to the top of the graph.
>
> My question is, are (1) and (2) possible with the current options
> available in ggplot2?

>

> Ramnath
>

I would suggest that you make a separate plot for the legend and use
grid and viewports to layout the separate plots. You will likely want
to use opts(legend.position = "none") for both plots. geom_tile might
be helpful for laying out the legend plot. Something to get you started:

af = data.frame(x=2.5:11,y=rep(1,9))
ggplot(af) + aes(x,y,fill=x) + geom_tile() +
opts(legend.position="none", title="US Jobless Rate")

I don't know of a clean way to move the x-axis to the top of the graph.
